title: Interpretation 17-10 (City of Bellingham): five-story wood-framed building with pressurized stair shafts, a Group B or M first floor, and CLT in Type IV exterior walls
jurisdiction: Washington State, requested by City of Bellingham (comparative test only; not Alberta)
code_edition: 2015 International Building Code, Sections 504, 602.1 and 602.4, with Washington amendment to 504.4.1, as cited

facts.text: Document type: State Building Code Council interpretation 17-10, one page; requester City of Bellingham.

Premise stated in the question: five stories of wood-framed construction are allowed where stair shafts are pressurized and the building is fully sprinklered to NFPA 13; occupancies in five-story wood are limited to residential uses.
Question 1 asks whether the first floor of such a building may be Group B or Group M.
Question 2 asks whether the story increase may also apply to a Type IV building.
Question 3 asks whether cross-laminated timber (CLT) classifies as Type IV construction.

limitations: The PDF contains the Council answer on the same page; do not present it as applicant-side input without flagging leakage.
No drawings, height or area calculations, or fire and life-safety design are in the record.
Edition as cited (2015 IBC with Washington amendments).
